newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end on holiday high note.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end on holiday high note.

text.p: Singapore shares closed higher on Thursday ahead of the Lunar New Year festivities which started with a midday close to the week's trading.
The stock market will be closed on Friday and Monday.
"It was a positive morning," said one local dealer.
Singapore's key Straits Times Industrials Index helped give the market its own version of the traditional good fortune gifts, rising 7.61 points to 2,203.39 at the 0430 GMT close.
Volume was a reasonable 151.5 million shares producing 221 gainers against 81 losers.
Malaysian over-the-counter stocks were the most active.
Actives were led by MBF Holdings, up four cents to Singapore $0.865 on traded volume of 24.1 million shares. FACB and Promet were also among the most traded counters.
The party mood permeating the stock market helped lift Asia Pacific Breweries to the top of the gainers list, up 45 cents to S$8.30, but with low volume.

Shares in Creative Technology continued their roller-coaster ride to end the day as the biggest loser down 40 cents at S$19.20. Creative's shares have alternately been the market's biggest gainer and loser each day this week.
